newsitem.title: USA: New lead prosecutor named in Oklahoma bombing case.
newsitem.headline: New lead prosecutor named in Oklahoma bombing case.

text.p: An assistant U.S. attorney from Indianapolis has been appointed as the new chief prosecutor in the Oklahoma City bombing case, the Justice Department said Thursday.
Larry Mackey replaces Joseph Hartzler who recently returned to his duties as an assistant U.S. attorney in Springfield, Ill.

Hartzler oversaw the prosecution of Timothy McVeigh for the 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City, which resulted in 168 deaths. McVeigh was sentenced to death by a federal jury in Denver earlier this month.
Mackey will be in charge of prosecuting McVeigh's co-defendant Terry Nichols, who was expected to go on trial this fall.
Mackey was second in command on Hartzler's team and also had planned to return to his previous duties, but recently changed his mind after talking with Attorney General Janet Reno, a source said.
He decided to stay on in part because the McVeigh trial took less time than expected, and because his wife and their two sons had already moved to Denver to be with him.
